requirements.quote: A client MUST authenticate the identity of the server.
requirements.condition: When a client establishes a QUIC connection with a server
requirements.required_behavior: The client authenticates the server's identity.
requirements.why_checkable: A handshake test can present valid and invalid server identities and observe whether the client performs authentication before accepting the peer.

requirements.quote:
A server MUST NOT use post-handshake client authentication (as
   defined in Section 4.6.2 of [TLS13])
requirements.condition: After the TLS handshake has completed
requirements.why_checkable: Server TLS state transitions and post-handshake traffic can be inspected to verify that the post-handshake authentication procedure is never initiated or used.

requirements.quote:
More specifically, servers MUST NOT send post-
   handshake TLS CertificateRequest messages
requirements.condition: After the TLS handshake has completed
requirements.why_checkable: Captured post-handshake TLS messages can be decoded to assert that no CertificateRequest is sent by the server.

requirements.quote:
clients MUST treat
   receipt of such messages as a connection error of type
   PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.condition: When a client receives a post-handshake TLS CertificateRequest message
requirements.required_behavior: Treat receipt as a connection error.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Continue the connection as though the post-handshake CertificateRequest were valid.
requirements.error_behavior: Close or fail the connection with error type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.why_checkable: A peer can inject a post-handshake CertificateRequest and verify that the client terminates the connection with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
